Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++/wxWidgets). The shell harness drives the real app with a mock AI model; the prompt recorder records, at each scripted point of a project chat, the app's real answers to a fixed list of reads so an offline eval runner can replay them. On 2026-11-12 commit 5e173c5e15 fixed every other harness mode; the recorder's three slice-time points are what is left. Build rules for this shared Mac are in AGENTS.md (check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`, build with -j4 or less, one build per build directory). The recorder takes 9 to 13 minutes per run.

Task:
The shell harness's prompt recorder (`--project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json <out.json>`, code in `tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`, run by `JusPrinShellHarness` from target `shell_integration_harness`) fails 3 checks in a row of runs on jusprin-dev at 5e173c5e15: `after-slice_answer_slice_report_has_its_result`, `print-hook-after-slice_answer_printer_list_has_its_result`, `print-hook-plan-slice_answer_printer_list_has_its_result`. At those three points the turn's own slice is still running. `ToolExecutionCoordinator::refuse_slice_poll` answers a `slice_report`, or a `workspace_inspect` asking for the slicing section, with "busy" until that slice ends, and the recorder now keeps that answer. But if the slice ends partway through the point's reads, the app starts the turn that tells the slice's outcome, the next request no longer carries the call's result, and the recorder fails. How far those points get depends on machine speed and load.

Task: make those three points record the same answers every run. First find out whether the harness can keep the slice from ending until the point's reads are done (or another way to make the timing fixed), and which answers those points should hold given what the app really tells the model in that turn ("busy"). If the right answer is a product or eval-data decision, stop and ask Kenneth in full before changing it. Then re-record `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`: the committed one predates the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge (object ids and the settings list differ at every point, about 7 more recorded answers per point), and `tests/project_prompt/README.md` keeps a log of every re-recording, so add an entry saying what changed. Do not run the live eval suite against a paid model without asking Kenneth first.

Done looks like: two back-to-back recorder runs pass with 0 failures and produce the same `requests.json` apart from ids and timestamps; the runner's schema test still passes; README updated; one commit on its own branch, not pushed.

# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each case names its request in requests.json and, in its docstring, the
# sentence of projectInstructions.ts it tests (line numbers at 6b4b8b6188).
# check() returns PASS, FAIL, UNOBSERVED or CONTINUE with a detail. CONTINUE
# is a read the case does not decide on: when it decides on none of a
# response's reads, the runner answers them all from the recording and asks
# again. UNOBSERVED is a step the case can say nothing about, or a read with
# no recorded answer, or the model still reading after MAX_READS answers.
# ANSWER_CHANGE: the step is a change the case decides on by what comes after it
# (a setup_record with a plan and no purpose, a slice_start). NEXT_TURN: the
# reply ended the turn undecided while a slice ran, and the case decides on the
# turn the slice's end starts. Case.later says what the run can follow: for each
# run of those so far (self.done), the point recorded right after it, in a
# conversation with the same start. The change's result and the reads after it
# come from that point.
SLICE_END = "the slice's end"


class Case:
    slice is now out of date. When to act: a print request is "verified by a
    slice whose findings you have read before you call it ready". Passes on
    slice_start, or a reply that does not claim the print is ready (judged)."""

    name = "after-apply"
    expected = "slice_start"


class AfterSlice(Readiness):
    """The prepare turn after slice_start started a run. Its result says the
    run goes on in the background, the person watches it in a card below
    the call, slice_report returns valid: false until it ends, and the app
    starts a new turn with the outcome when it ends after this turn. A reply
    that does not claim readiness is what that invites. The recorded reads were
    taken one after another while the run went on: workspace_inspect shows
    it still slicing, and slice_report returns valid: false or the finished
    slice, depending on whether the run had ended when it was recorded.
    A model that polls workspace_inspect gets that same in-flight answer
    each time, so it ends unobserved at MAX_READS. The same sentences as after-apply.
    Passes on slice_report, or a reply that does not claim the print is
    ready (judged)."""

    name = "after-slice"
    expected = "slice_report"


# The reads that check a setup against a purpose, as the setup skill names
# them (skills/project-setup-changed/SKILL.md).
SETUP_CHECKS = ("settings_get", "presets_list", "printer_setup_preview")
READY_QUESTION = ("Does the assistant's last message say or imply that the print is ready to print or to send to the "
                  "printer?")


class AfterIntent(Case):
    """The prepare turn after setup_record recorded "PETG, strong" as the
    first purpose; its result states the purpose and the setup in force
    (Bambu PLA Basic), and the request ends with the setup skill
    (skills/project-setup-changed/SKILL.md): "check that the printer,
    filament, process and plate type in force suit the purpose recorded
    now", with settings_get, presets_list and printer_setup_preview. Passes
    on one of those three; fails on slice_start or a reply claiming the
    if providers:
        body["provider"] = {"order": providers, "allow_fallbacks": False}
    return body


def recorded_answer(name, step):
    """The result the app gave at this point for the read the model asked
    for, or None.
    - workspace_inspect and slice_report: the recording with every section,
      whichever sections the model named;
    - settings_get: each key asked for, in the order asked, taken from the
      recorded reads of the same scope and target -- its item, or the app's
      unknownKeys entry for a name it does not know -- with the rest of the
      first such result; None if any key was not recorded;
    - settings_search: the recording of the same scope, target, query
      (case, spacing and word order aside) and changedOnly, whatever limit or
      writable the model gave; not for a cursor;
    - object_analyze: the recording for that object and session, with every
      include but measure, whichever the model named; not with measure or
      candidates;
    - skill_read: the recording of the same skill;
    - view_render: the recording of the same plate (none named: the active
      plate) and view (iso when none is named), whatever size the model
      asked for. The recording keeps the result's text only: the pinned hosts
      refuse any request with an image, so the picture the app sends after
      the result is never replayed."""
    answers = [answer for answer in REQUESTS[name]["answers"] if answer["tool"] == step.tool]
    arguments = step.arguments
    if step.tool in ("workspace_inspect", "printer_list"):
        return answers[0]["output"] if answers else None
    if step.tool == "skill_read":
        return next((answer["output"] for answer in answers if answer["arguments"] == arguments), None)
    if step.tool == "object_analyze":
        if "measure" in arguments.get("include", []) or "candidates" in arguments or "measure" in arguments:
            return None
        for answer in answers:
            if answer["arguments"]["objectId"] == arguments.get("objectId") and \
                    answer["arguments"]["sessionId"] == arguments.get("sessionId"):
                return answer["output"]
        return None
    if step.tool == "view_render":
        for answer in answers:
            if answer["arguments"].get("plateId") == arguments.get("plateId") and \
                    answer["arguments"].get("view", "iso") == arguments.get("view", "iso"):
                return answer["output"]
        return None
    if step.tool == "slice_report":
        for answer in answers:
            if arguments.get("plateId") in (None, json.loads(answer["output"])["result"].get("plateId")):
                return answer["output"]
        return None
    target = arguments.get("target") or {}
    same = [answer for answer in answers if answer["arguments"].get("scope") == arguments.get("scope") and
            (answer["arguments"].get("target") or {}) == target]
    if step.tool == "settings_get":
        items, unknown, base = {}, {}, None

            output = json.loads(answer["output"])
            base = base or output
            for item in output["result"]["items"]:
                items.setdefault(item["key"], item)
            for entry in output["result"].get("unknownKeys", []):
                unknown.setdefault(entry["key"], entry)
        keys = list(dict.fromkeys(arguments.get("keys") or []))
        if base is None or not keys or any(key not in items and key not in unknown for key in keys):

def answers_for(name, step, refused=None, done=(), plan=None, answering=None):
    """The results the app would give the calls of one response, in order,
    or None when one the app would run has no recorded answer. As the app
    does, a refused call (refused: its index and result) gets the refusal,
    and a call after one that did not succeed is answered without being
    run. Reads come from the point after what the run has done (done), with
    the model's plan if it wrote one (plan: its arguments). answering is the
    index among the calls of the change the case asked to have answered: it
    and every read after it are answered from the point after that change."""
    later = CASES[name].later
    point = later.get(done, name)
    results, failed = [], None
    for index, read in enumerate(step.each_read()):
        if failed:
            results.append(not_run(failed))
            continue
        if refused and index == refused[0]:
            results.append(refused[1])
            failed = read
            continue
        if index == answering:
            point = later[done + (read.tool,)]
            plan = read.arguments if read.tool == "setup_record" else plan
            answer = last_output(point)
        else:
            answer = recorded_answer(point, read)
        if answer is None:
            return None, read
        results.append(answer if plan is None else with_plan(point, answer, plan))
        if json.loads(answer).get("state") != "succeeded":
            failed = read
    return results, None


def last_output(point):
    """The last call's result in a recorded request, byte for byte."""
    return next(item["output"] for item in reversed(REQUESTS[point]["body"]["input"])
                if item.get("type") == "function_call_output")

checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`; `slice_report` of the
  active plate (no plate named) and of every plate by its `plateId`;
- `skill_read` of each skill the page lists for it (the calibration skill,
  today), given for that name;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- a `changedOnly` `settings_search` with an empty query of every object on
  every plate (its own changed settings), given for that object whatever
  `limit` the model passed; Opus 5.5 sends it first in the file-loaded and
  print-this cases;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed. A search with `changedOnly` is
  answered only by a recorded search with it, and one without by one
  without; never one with a `cursor`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 34
points took 9 to 13 minutes on an M-series Mac in 2026-11. At the three
points recorded while the turn's own slice runs (`after-slice`,
`print-hook-after-slice`, `print-hook-plan-slice`), a slice report or a read
of the slicing section is answered "busy" until that slice ends, and the
recorder keeps that answer; if the slice ends partway through the reads, the
app starts the turn that tells its outcome and the recorder loses the rest,
so how far those points get depends on the machine's speed. To keep
`requests.json` small (about
6 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer. The first `--backend claude-cli` batch (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-19)
left 10 of 63 runs unobserved, nearly all on two reads DeepSeek V4 Flash
never sent: a `changedOnly` search of each object and `slice_report` of a
plate other than the active one. With both recorded, the six cases that
sent them (`file-note-not-instructions`, `print-this-no-purpose`,
`model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool`, `model-opened-by-tool`,
`slice-refused-then-ready`) ran 3 times each on the subscription with no
unobserved run; `print-this-no-purpose` failed all three, on an
`intent_update` with a purpose the model assumed.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

person's words, the scripted calls, and three assistant replies (the summary
after the prepare turn, the first message about an opened file, and the first
message about the wall hook). The

## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 81 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 2 when nothing was judged (there is no baseline,
or the run's model, host or judge differs from the baseline's), 0 otherwise;
`--must-pass N` makes the exit code 1 when a case passes fewer than N runs
instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.


All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by

"record" removed. Usage: split_script.py script.json outdir point..."""
import copy
import json
import sys

outdir = sys.argv[2]

    found = None
    for conversation in script["conversations"]:
        records = [r.get("record") for s in conversation["steps"] for r in s.get("replies", [])]
        if point in records:
            found = copy.deepcopy(conversation)
    assert found, point
    for step in found["steps"]:
        for reply in step.get("replies", []):
            if reply.get("record") != point:
                reply.pop("record", None)
                reply.pop("skill", None)
    one = dict(script)
    one["conversations"] = [found]
    with open(f"{outdir}/{point}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(one, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)

Prompt recorder: hold the turn's slice open so its three slice-time points record the same answers

Three points of the shell harness's prompt recorder (after-slice,
print-hook-after-slice, print-hook-plan-slice) are recorded right after a
scripted slice_start, while that slice runs. The app answers a slice_report,
or a workspace_inspect asking for the slicing section, "busy" in that turn
and ends the turn at the third such answer. The recorder's first three
reads are all of that kind, so a slice still running at the third ended the
turn and the next read failed; a slice that ended sooner left the later
reads with the finished slice. What a point held depended on machine speed.

The recorder now holds back OrcaSlicer's end-of-slice event
(EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED, through a wxEventFilter) from the scripted
slice_start until the request after it is answered, so the slice counts as
running for all of that request's reads. Once a slice_report comes back
busy it calls no other, since the app gives every plate the same answer;
and it reads workspace_inspect again without the slicing section, for a
model that asks only for the others. The offline runner answers any plate's
slice_report with a busy one and gives that slicing-free read to a model
that names sections but not slicing.
